cards.b: CNS: brain and spinal cord. PNS: the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord.
Coordination and regulation of body functions.
Carries impulses from a receptor to the CNS.
Inside the CNS; carries impulses from sensory neurone to motor neurone.
Carries impulses from the CNS to an effector.
Stimulus → receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector → response.
A means of automatically and rapidly integrating and coordinating stimuli with the responses of effectors (muscles and glands).
They are automatic and rapid, so they protect the body from damage.
Groups of receptor cells responding to specific stimuli: light, sound, touch, temperature, chemicals.
A chemical substance, produced by a gland and carried by the blood, which alters the activity of one or more specific target organs.
Adrenal glands: adrenaline. Pancreas: insulin (and glucagon). Testes: testosterone. Ovaries: oestrogen.
Increased breathing rate, increased heart rate, increased pupil diameter.

cards.f: Why are the effects of adrenaline useful?
cards.b: More oxygen and glucose reach muscles for respiration, releasing more energy for action.

gaps.s: The brain and spinal cord make up the ___ nervous system.

A muscle or gland that carries out a response is called an ___ .
Hormones are carried around the body in the ___ .
Adrenaline is secreted by the ___ glands.
Adrenaline makes the pupils ___ in diameter.
Hormones are secreted by ___ glands directly into the blood.

short.q: Describe the pathway of a simple reflex arc when a hand touches a hot object. [4]
short.model: Temperature receptors in the skin detect the stimulus, a sensory neurone carries impulses to a relay neurone in the spinal cord, then a motor neurone carries impulses to the arm muscle (effector), which contracts.

short.q: Explain why a reflex action protects the body. [2]
short.model: It is automatic and rapid, so the response happens before the brain has time to think, preventing damage.

short.q: State two differences between nervous and hormonal communication. [2]
short.model: Nerves send electrical impulses along neurones; hormones are chemicals carried in the blood to target organs.
points: impulses along neurones versus chemicals in blood
hormones act on specific target organs

short.q: State three effects of adrenaline and explain why they help in a dangerous situation. [3]
short.model: Faster breathing, faster heart rate and wider pupils; more oxygen and glucose reach muscles so more energy is released for action.
points: increased pupil diameter / more oxygen and glucose to muscles

short.q: A student's reaction time is measured by catching a falling ruler. State two variables to keep constant. [2]
short.model: Use the same hand and the same starting position of the fingers; the same person drops the ruler with no warning.
